Treatment summary
Patient presents following a rear-end motor vehicle collision with ongoing neck and low back strain. Over the course of 30 visits,
care has consisted of manual therapy, progressive range-of-motion and stabilization exercises, and periodic reassessment.
Reported symptoms have been consistent across visits, and the patient has been compliant with the home program. Palpation
reveals paraspinal muscle tenderness and mild guarding in the cervical and lumbar regions, and some provocative maneuvers
reproduce pain, while several other neurological and orthopedic screening tests are within normal limits. The patient describes
the imapct as minor, and the severity of the reported complaints appears greater than the mechanism of injury would typically
predict. Treatment has extended somewhat beyond the typical course for this type of strain. No prior injury to the cervical or
lumbar region is documented in available records. Billing reviewed for this episode reflects single charges for each service
without duplication. Prognosis is guarded to fair, with continued reassessment planned.
